extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP/AI working on story evaluation and generation
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating LLM-based evaluators for narrative/story quality and using them as reward models to improve story generation. Emphasis on pairwise reasoning, chain-of-thought data synthesis, multi-agent filtering, and benchmark validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in pairwise comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounded in pairwise comparison, the framework first self-synthesizes score-aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) data via a multi-persona strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pairwise comparisons (relative judgments between story pairs) as the primary evaluation signal rather than absolute scores; this grounding supports generating coherent, score-aligned explanatory reasoning and is the foundation for downstream evaluator training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-synthesized score-aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) data
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework self-synthesizes score-aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate explanatory CoTs that are explicitly aligned with numeric or ordinal scores so the evaluator learns not only final ratings but the reasoning that justifies those ratings; synthetic CoTs are used as training data for the evaluator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-persona strategy for diverse reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework employs a multi-persona strategy when self-synthesizing CoT data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt multiple personas or perspectives when producing evaluation rationales to increase diversity and coverage of plausible judgments and to reduce bias from a single evaluative viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-filtering via multi-agents to ensure logical rigor and robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure data quality, these raw CoTs undergo a self-filtering process, utilizing multi-agents to guarantee their logical rigor and robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply multi-agent review/verification to filter or refine synthetic CoTs so that retained explanations are logically rigorous and robust; this quality-control step is essential before training the evaluator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluator trained on refined data and deployed as a reward model
rubrics_metrics.description: Finally, the evaluator trained on the refined data is deployed as a reward model to guide the story generation task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train a dedicated evaluator on the filtered, score-aligned CoT dataset and use it as a reward signal for generative models (e.g., RL/fine-tuning) to steer generation toward higher-quality stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark evaluation (StoryER, HANNA, OpenMEVA) / SOTA performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on three evaluation benchmarks including StoryER, HANNA and OpenMEVA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate evaluator performance against established story-evaluation benchmarks (StoryER, HANNA, OpenMEVA); benchmark metrics and improvements are primary evidence of evaluator quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation quality improvement when used as reward model
rubrics_metrics.description: When served as a reward model, it significantly enhances the quality of generated stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the impact of the evaluator-as-reward-model on generation quality (automatic metrics and/or human evaluations); improvement in generated-story quality is an intended outcome and evaluation target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for adaptability and rigorous reasoning in evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing methods face a dilemma: prompt engineering for closed-source models suffers from poor adaptability, while fine-tuning approaches for open-source models lack the rigorous reasoning capabilities essential for story evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluators that balance adaptability (work across models/contexts) and rigorous chain-of-thought reasoning; avoid approaches that are brittle to prompts or that produce shallow/ungrounded judgments.
